extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys, national patent offices, Contracting States and European Patent Office officials
extracted.subtask_description: Explanatory and normative provisions of the European Patent Convention covering administrative rules, finance, patentability criteria (novelty, inventive step, industrial application), procedural filing requirements, divisional/forwarding rules, translation and effects of publication/grant/revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of office for elected Board members
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of office of the members elected by the Administrative Council shall be three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This term of office shall not be renewable. The Board shall perform duties given by the Administrative Council in accordance with the Rules of Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convening and frequency of Administrative Council meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings of the Administrative Council shall be convened by its Chairman and the Administrative Council shall hold an ordinary meeting once each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President of the European Patent Office shall take part in deliberations. Additional meetings may be held on the Chairman's initiative or at the request of one third of the Contracting States. Deliberations are based on an agenda and Rules of Procedure; provisional agenda includes any question requested by a Contracting State under the Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance of observers at Administrative Council
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO and other inter-governmental organisations with agreements shall be represented at Administrative Council meetings; other inter-governmental and international NGOs of interest may be invited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation is subject to provisions of agreements concluded with the Organisation; invitations may be extended for discussions of mutual interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages of the Administrative Council
rubrics_metrics.description: The languages in use in the deliberations of the Administrative Council shall be English, French and German.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents submitted and minutes shall be drawn up in those three languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of staff, premises and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Patent Office shall place at the disposal of the Administrative Council and any body established by it such staff, premises and equipment as necessary for performance of their duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational support is to be provided by the EPO to Administrative Council bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Council competence to amend Convention provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Council shall be competent to amend the time limits laid down in this Convention (with restrictions) and the Implementing Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment of time limits applies to Article 94 only under Article 95 conditions. The Council's competence extends to adoption/amendment of Financial Regulations, Service Regulations, Pension Scheme Regulations, Rules relating to Fees, and its Rules of Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Council competence on examining division composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Council may decide, in the light of experience, that in certain categories Examining Divisions shall consist of one technical examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such decisions may be rescinded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to negotiate and conclude agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Council may authorise the President of the European Patent Office to negotiate and, with its approval, to conclude agreements on behalf of the Organisation with States and organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes agreements with documentation centres and intergovernmental organisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting rights in the Administrative Council
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to vote in the Administrative Council is restricted to the Contracting States; each Contracting State shall have one vote (subject to Article 36).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting entitlement limited to Contracting States; weighting rules may apply for certain decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting rules and majorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions (other than specified exceptions) are taken by a simple majority of Contracting States represented and voting; certain important decisions require a three-quarters majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstentions are not considered votes. The three-quarters requirement applies to a listed set of Articles (e.g., Article 7, 11(1), 33, 39(1), 40(2&4), etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted second ballot for fees/budget decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: For adoption/amendment of Rules relating to Fees and budget decisions that would increase financial contributions, a Contracting State may require a second ballot with weighted votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second ballot votes are calculated: percentage from special financial contributions scale × number of Contracting States ÷ 5, rounded up, plus five additional votes; cap of 30 votes per State. First ballot is one vote per State; result determined by second ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources covering Organisation's expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisation's expenditure shall be covered by (a) the Organisation's own resources, (b) payments by Contracting States in respect of renewal fees for European patents levied in those States, (c) special financial contributions, and (d) where appropriate, revenue provided for in Article 146.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple funding sources defined; ensures budget financing modalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisation's own resources defined
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organisation's own resources are the yield from the fees laid down in this Convention, and also all receipts, whatever their nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All fee income and receipts count toward own resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payments by Contracting States in respect of renewal fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting State shall pay to the Organisation for each renewal fee received an amount equal to a proportion of that fee (not exceeding 75%) fixed by the Administrative Council; the proportion shall be the same for all Contracting States but a uniform minimum may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must communicate necessary information; due dates determined by Administrative Council; interest payable on unpaid amounts after due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of fees and special financial contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts of fees and the proportion payable by States shall be fixed to ensure revenue sufficient to balance the budget; if insufficient, Contracting States shall remit special financial contributions determined by the Administrative Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special contributions are determined for an accounting period based on historic patent application filing numbers (one half proportional to applications filed in that State; one half proportional to the second highest number of applications filed in other States by residents of that State); special rules for States with >25,000 filings. Repayment rules with interest and ordering of repayments specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advances from Contracting States
rubrics_metrics.description: At the President's request, Contracting States shall make advances on account of their payments and contributions within limits fixed by the Administrative Council, apportioned in proportion to amounts due for the accounting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 39(3&4) rules apply mutatis mutandis to advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Income and expenditure shall be estimated for each accounting period and shown in the budget; the budget shall be balanced and drawn up in the unit of account fixed in the Financial Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amending or supplementary budgets may be created if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorisation and carry-forward of appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenditure entered in the budget shall be authorised for one accounting period; appropriations (other than staff costs) unexpended may be carried forward but not beyond the end of the following accounting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriations set out under different headings and subdivided per Financial Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations for unforeseeable expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget may contain appropriations for unforeseeable expenditure whose employment is subject to prior approval of the Administrative Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows contingency funds under Council control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting period defined
rubrics_metrics.description: The accounting period shall commence on 1 January and end on 31 December.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard annual accounting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and adoption of the budget
rubrics_metrics.description: The President shall lay the draft budget before the Administrative Council not later than the date prescribed in the Financial Regulations; the budget and any amending or supplementary budgets shall be adopted by the Administrative Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal adoption process by Council based on President's draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional budget authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If the budget is not adopted at the beginning of the accounting period, expenditures may be effected provisionally up to one twelfth of previous appropriations per month per heading, with possible authorisation for excesses by the Administrative Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional monthly payments continue; special financial contributions paid provisionally monthly per Article 40 scale; refund/payment continuity rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget implementation responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the European Patent Office shall implement the budget and any amending or supplementary budget on his own responsibility and within the limits of allocated appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within the budget, the President may transfer funds between headings subject to Financial Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditing of accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Income and expenditure account and balance sheet shall be examined by auditors whose independence is beyond doubt, appointed by the Administrative Council for five years (renewable/extensible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit based on vouchers, possibly in situ; auditors must verify lawful receipt/expenditure and sound financial management and shall draw up a report. President submits accounts and auditor's report annually; Administrative Council approves and grants discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the Financial Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial Regulations shall establish procedures for budget establishment/implementation/auditing; methods for payments and contributions; responsibilities of accounting/paying officers; rates of interest; method for calculating contributions under Article 146; and the composition/duties of a Budget and Finance Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial Regulations set the detailed financial governance framework and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules relating to Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules relating to Fees shall determine the amounts of the fees and the ways in which they are to be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed fee structure and payment mechanisms are handled by these Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (Article 52)
rubrics_metrics.description: European patents shall be granted for any inventions which are susceptible of industrial application, which are new and which involve an inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three cumulative requirements: industrial application, novelty, inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-inventions / exclusions (Article 52(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The following shall not be regarded as inventions: discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods; aesthetic creations; schemes, rules and methods for performing mental acts, playing games or doing business, and programs for computers; presentations of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are excluded only to the extent the application relates to them 'as such' (see Article 52(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion 'as such' (Article 52(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The exclusions listed are to exclude patentability only to the extent a European patent application or patent relates to such subject-matter or activities 'as such'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows patentability where technical contribution goes beyond the excluded subject-matter 'as such'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for treatment and diagnostic methods excluded (Article 52(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy and diagnostic methods practised on the human or animal body shall not be regarded as inventions susceptible of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion does not apply to products, in particular substances or compositions, for use in any of these methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to patentability (ordre public/morality and biological processes) (Article 53)
rubrics_metrics.description: European patents shall not be granted in respect of inventions the publication or exploitation of which would be contrary to ordre public or morality; and plant or animal varieties or essentially biological processes for the production of plants or animals (excluding microbiological processes and their products).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploitation being prohibited by law in some States does not by itself make it contrary to ordre public or morality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty – state of the art (Article 54)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is new if it does not form part of the state of the art. The state of the art comprises everything made available to the public by written or oral description, by use, or in any other way before the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, content of earlier European patent applications filed earlier but published under Article 93 on or after that date are part of the state of the art (Article 54(3)), subject to designation conditions (54(4)). Special rule preserves patentability of substances for use in methods excluded under Article 52(4) if such use was not in the state of the art (54(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosures / grace period (Article 55)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure occurring no earlier than six months before filing shall not be taken into consideration for novelty if due to evident abuse against the applicant or because the applicant displayed the invention at an official or officially recognised international exhibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For exhibition disclosures, the applicant must state at filing that the invention was displayed and file a supporting certificate within periods/conditions in the Implementing Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (Article 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention involves an inventive step if, having regard to the state of the art, it is not obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents within Article 54(3) (earlier-filed European applications published later) are not to be considered in deciding inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial application (Article 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is susceptible of industrial application if it can be made or used in any kind of industry, including agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the 'utility' requirement for patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a European patent application (Article 75/58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent application may be filed by any natural or legal person, or any body equivalent to a legal person by virtue of the law governing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple/joint applicants are permitted; applications may be filed at EPO Munich or The Hague branch, or at central industrial property office of a Contracting State if national law permits (same effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to the European patent (ownership rules) (Article 60)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to a European patent belongs to the inventor or his successor in title. For employee inventors the right is determined by the law of the State in which the employee is mainly employed (or employer's place of business if indeterminate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two or more persons made the invention independently, the right belongs to the person with the earliest filing date (subject to publication requirement and effect only for designated States in that application). For EPO proceedings, the applicant is deemed entitled to exercise the right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies where applicant not entitled (Article 61)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a final decision adjudges another person entitled to the grant, that person may within three months after final decision (and before grant) prosecute the application as his own, file a new application for the same invention, or request refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure, special conditions, and fee timelines for such actions are set in the Implementing Regulations; Article 76(1) applies mutatis mutandis to new application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of inventor to be mentioned (Article 62)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor shall have the right, vis-à-vis the applicant or proprietor, to be mentioned as such before the European Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral right to attribution in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of the European patent (Article 63)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of the European patent shall be 20 years as from the date of filing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting States may extend term under national conditions to account for war or similar emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred by a European patent (Article 64)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent shall, from the date of publication of the mention of its grant, in each Contracting State in respect of which it is granted, confer the same rights as a national patent in that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject-matter is a process, protection extends to products directly obtained by such process. Any infringement is dealt with by national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirements for specification (Article 65)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting State may require that if the text in which EPO intends to grant or maintain a patent is not in one of its official languages, the applicant/proprietor must supply a translation in one of its official languages (or prescribed language) within three months after the start of specified time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may require the applicant to pay publication translation costs. Failure to observe translation provisions may render the European patent void ab initio in that State. Corrected translations may be filed under conditions; good faith users may be protected in some circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of European filing with national filing (Article 66)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent application with an accorded date of filing is equivalent to a regular national filing in the designated Contracting States (where appropriate with the priority claimed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for establishing national filing rights from European filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional protection after publication of application (Article 67)
rubrics_metrics.description: From publication under Article 93, a European patent application provisionally confers upon the applicant such protection as conferred by Article 64 in designated Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may limit this protection but must ensure at least a claim for reasonable compensation for use between publication and grant. Non-official-language States may require translations of claims to be public or communicated to users. The effects never arise if the application is withdrawn, deemed withdrawn, or finally refused, or if a designation is withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of revocation (Article 68)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the European patent has been revoked in opposition proceedings, the application and resulting patent shall be deemed not to have had the effects specified in Articles 64 and 67 from the outset, to the extent of revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation retroactively removes effects conferred by publication/grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of protection and claim interpretation (Article 69)
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of protection conferred by a European patent or application shall be determined by the terms of the claims; nevertheless the description and drawings shall be used to interpret the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up to grant, protection is determined by the latest filed claims in the publication; the granted or amended patent determines retroactively the protection conferred by the application insofar as such protection is not thereby extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic text of the application/patent (Article 70)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text in the language of the proceedings shall be the authentic text in proceedings before the EPO and in any Contracting State. In certain cases the original text is the basis to determine extension beyond content as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting States may treat translations as authentic in that State (except in revocation proceedings), but must permit corrected translations and may protect users acting in good faith if translation correction narrows protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application requirements (Article 76)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European divisional application must be filed directly with the EPO Munich or The Hague branch and may be filed only in respect of subject-matter which does not extend beyond the content of the earlier application as filed; if complied with, it is deemed filed on the date of the earlier application and has the benefit of any right to priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The divisional shall not designate Contracting States not designated in the earlier application. Procedure, special conditions and fee time limits set in Implementing Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding of national-filed European applications (Article 77)
rubrics_metrics.description: Central industrial property offices shall forward European patent applications filed with them to the EPO in the shortest time compatible with national secrecy laws. Applications not liable to secrecy shall be forwarded within six weeks; those requiring secrecy examination shall be forwarded within four months after filing or fourteen months if priority claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications made secret shall not be forwarded. Applications not reaching the EPO before the end of the fourteenth month after filing (or priority date) shall be deemed withdrawn and filing, search and designation fees refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing locations and national filing equivalence (Article 75)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent application may be filed at the EPO (Munich or The Hague) or, if national law permits, at a Contracting State's central industrial property office or other competent authority; an application filed with a national authority shall have the same effect as if filed at the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not preclude national laws that require initial national filing or restrict communication abroad for certain inventions (secrecy). No Contracting State may allow filing of European divisional applications with a national authority.
